knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parabola

question.:question/problem:
![](images/88/88bec66b7ece961f2f0fc4083ce317f2bdc414e0a219d61bbf9bf73ae667ca0f.png)

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the left-opening parabola shown above.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola has its vertex at $O,$ and passes through the point $(-2,2).$

The general equation of a left- or right-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(0,0)$ is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Substituting $x=-2$ and $y=2$ into the equation above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(2)^{2} & =4p(-2) \\ 4 & =-8p \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of our parabola is 

$$
{y}^{2}=-2x.
$$

Finally, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2x) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-2 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

The general equation of a left- or right-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(0,0)$ is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Substituting $x=-2$ and $y=-5$ into the equation above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-5)^{2} & =4p(-2) \\ 25 & =-8p \\ p & =-\frac{25}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of our parabola is 

$$
{y}^{2}=-\frac{25}{2}x.
$$

Finally, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\frac{25}{2}x) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{25}{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{25}{4y}\end{aligned}
$$
